$schema_note: Machine-readable spec of the PF.Magic 'Ballz' pet-rendering technique (Ballz 1994 -> Dogz 1995 / Catz 1996). provenance: read_out = disassembled from the original engine by the dogz-reverse project; measured = observed pixel/file data; inferred = their inference; ours = choice made in this reimplementation.
caveat: The petz.js/dogz-reverse kb used here documents Dogz (1995) in depth. Catz (1996) runs on the same engine and its binary is widely archived; catz-recomp (github.com/sp00nznet/catz-recomp) has statically recompiled the whole CATZDLL.DLL engine to playable C, and the Petz hexing community has mapped cat breedfiles (LNZ) for years. Cat-specific rules in this file were not taken from those sources yet, so treat them as extrapolated until checked against them.
style_elements: Body = flat-filled circles in 3D, sorted far-to-near, no gradients, no lighting
Thick tapered 'linez' join balls (ears, tail, legs, snout) and carry the first ball's color
Fur = ragged row-starts (fuzz) + one stray pixel per row in the upper half (speckle)
Outlines are partial: a single left-edge pixel ('half outline') or N-px rim; never a vector stroke
Coat colors come from 6-shade palette ramps; the speckle is the mirror shade in the same ramp
Eyes = ball + separately drawn iris that eases toward a look-target, clamped inside the eye; eyelid = cut circle in coat color
Low frame rate (~22 fps) and integer pixels; reads as chunky, hand-made, alive
Pet walks on the actual desktop; cursor is the hand (pet, poke, scruff, give)

pipeline.detail: One shared skeleton per species (Dogz: 65 balls). Animations store only 3D ball centers per frame; breed files store only looks.

coord' = coord * petScale >> 8; radius = size * ballScale >> 9. Scales interpolate puppy->adult by age: age*(adult-puppy)/100 + puppy. Puppy: positions 140/256, balls 200/256 (smaller body, bigger balls).
Yaw about the vertical axis by facing; then pitch tilt = -7 - |64 - |yaw|| / 10 (angles in 1/256 turn): 13 when facing viewer, 7 side-on.
Orthographic: x across, y down, larger z farther.
Every ball and line drawn in depth order, farthest first. A line's depth = average of its two ends.
A held object is drawn as a per-ball callback right after its anchor ball (chin/paw), so nearer balls overdraw it.

circle_table.detail: For each diameter d in 1..119: row width w(r) = sqrt(d^2 - (d - 2r)^2), r = 1..d. Plus a fixed random spot per row (speckle position) and 8 fuzz tables of row-start shifts.

modes.-1: no outline: fill each row in ball color; each row in the upper half gets 1 pixel at a random x (from the fixed table) in the speckle color
modes.0: half outline: same as -1, plus each row's leftmost pixel in outline color
modes.>0: outline N px thick: top N rows fully outline color, then N px of outline at each end of every row; no speckles
modes.-2: partial circle cut along an angled line (eyelids)
modes.-4: fill from a color ramp down the rows (eyes)

fuzz.detail: Level picks a table that shifts each row's start right by a random 0..7 px; row width unchanged. Fixed per diameter, so the raggedness is stable, not flickering.

speckle_color.detail: s = first index of c's ramp, R = ramp length (6). Reflects the shade within its ramp: shade k -> shade R-1-k.

shading.detail: None. Each ball is one flat palette index.

line.detail: Drawn in the first ball's color. Each end's thickness = that ball's radius * 256/300. LNZ row: start ball, end ball, fuzz.
line.ours: Scanline-filled tapered quad with per-row fuzz shift and 1-px edge pixels in outline color, so it matches the ball raster.

eye.iris_position: relative to eye from frame, or toward a look-target, or centered (by state); eased 0.6 px/frame; clamped per axis to eyeRadius - 0.8*irisRadius
eye.iris_fill: flat iris color, no fuzz/speckle/outline; if iris > 7 px across, inset 2 px and refill in pupil color
eye.eyelid: covering share of the eye by a circle cut along a line at the angle between the eyes, in eyelid color
eye.ours: cat pupils are vertical slits whose width tracks excitement

breed_file_LNZ.syntax: Windows profile style [Section] headers; one line per entry; values comma-separated before first tab; after tab = comment
other_sections: Default Scales (adult pet, adult ball, young pet, young ball)
later_versions: Add Ball (extra balls anchored to skeleton)

animation.BHD: header: ball count, per-ball diameters, animation count, per-animation end-frame, per-frame byte offsets
animation.BDT: per frame: bbox (6 words), flags (1 sequence start, 2 end), then x,y,z signed words per ball, then up to 6 (ball, signed byte) extras
animation.frame_rate: a frame every 45 ms at most (~22 fps)
animation.ours: No original animation data is used. Poses are procedural (gait cycles, sit, loaf, groom, stalk, pounce, beg, scruffed) and eased toward each frame, which plays the role of BDT keyframes.

behavior.provenance: read_out (Dogz PetModule), adapted to cats by us
behavior.structure: state machine pushing scripts onto a queue; every choice is rand() % n
behavior.personality: 11 factors 1..100, each = center moved by spread - sqrt(rand() % spread^2) (clusters near center)
behavior.excitement: 100 * ((1 + sin(phi + pi*t/24000)) / 2) ^ ((100 - c)/25), t in 17 ms ticks: about a 13-minute mood cycle; calm breeds spend longer low
behavior.idle_plan: rand() % (13 - e/10) + 6 - e/20 items; each a trick if rand()%100 <= e else 1-4 runs of pants/look-abouts; then sleep if rand()%30+30 > e else wander
behavior.locomotion: walk/trot/run index = ((rand()%21 + e - 10) * 3) / 100; target >= 400 px away, 60 px inside stage edges; turn rate 6/256 turn per frame
behavior.petting: button held over pet 4 frames with movement = stroke; preferred spot chest 20 / belly 30 / rump 50; enjoyment accumulates to 16; high enjoyment + calm -> roll/sleep
behavior.poke: click on face/leg/tail without stroking -> flinch/snap; annoyance factor +5
behavior.ball_physics: held: velocity = half cursor delta; released: lose 1/40 speed per frame, stop < 1 px/frame, bounce off stage edges; pet steers at position 4 frames ahead
behavior.hit_test: balls tested nearest first, each as a square as wide as drawn; each ball maps to a body region (head, face, legs, tail, chest/belly, rump)

ours_habitat.silhouette_pass: Bo only: balls/lines drawn without rims into an offscreen buffer, then one 1px outline around the whole cat's alpha
ours_habitat.curls: Bo only: rex coat as staggered 2px dash rows every 3rd ball row, one shade darker
ours_habitat.pod_clip: cat inside the pod is clipped to the opening ellipse; the pod's lower lip is drawn after the cat
ours_habitat.habitat: stage-bounded world; jungle scene painted with the same raster vocabulary (scanline polys, row-filled ellipses, speckles)
